To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) generative replay is beneficial for continual learning, (ii) dual memory is beneficial for continual lifelong learning and (iii) the proposed architecture provides insights into the connection between sleep, memory and learning.

(i) generative replay is better than replay of random samples, (ii) a dual memory architecture with generative replay is more efficient than a single memory architecture, and (iii), our architecture provides insights on the human memory and learning.

(i) we propose a novel dual memory architecture that emulates the complementary learning systems in the human brain, (ii) we demonstrate the benefits of dual memory and generative replay, and (iii), we provide insights on the connection of sleep and learning in the brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a deep neural network that can emulate human memory, and in doing so, learn continuously and retain knowledge of past tasks.
developing a deep learning architecture that is capable of learning continuously and retaining knowledge over time.
developing a deep learning architecture that can learn continuously, while retaining the ability to learn from new tasks and avoid catastrophic forgetting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our architecture is the first of its kind that is capable of continual learning and averts catastrophic forgetting in deep neural networks.
we have developed an architecture that can learn continuously from sequentially incoming data, while averting the problem of catastrophic forgetting.
our work provides the first deep generative dual memory network capable of continually learning from sequentially presented data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel deep generative dual memory network for continual learning that can maintain performance on learnt sequential tasks, while learning continuously from new tasks.
we propose a deep neural architecture with a generative replay mechanism that can be trained to learn continuously from sequentially incoming data.
we have developed an architecture for continual learning that is inspired by the dual memory architecture and the complementary learning systems in humans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human brain has evolved to be capable of continual learning and that artificial neural networks should be able to do the same.
continual learning is not a matter of capacity, but rather of memory architecture.
generative replay can be used to alleviate catastrophic forgetting in continual learning and that the dual memory architecture is crucial in maintaining performance on learnt tasks.
